title: The Adventures of Sam Spade
paragraphs: Dashiell Hammett's private detective Sam Spade, played most famously by Howard Duff, recounts hard-boiled cases filled with murder, deception, eccentric suspects, and sharply comic dialogue.
Hard-boiled detective series built around Dashiell Hammett’s Sam Spade, with a more comic and self-aware radio characterization.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: ABC summer series (July 12, 1946 to October 4, 1946) on [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]], CBS regular series (September 29, 1946 to September 25, 1949) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], NBC Howard Duff era (October 2, 1949 to September 17, 1950) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], and NBC Steve Dunne revival (November 17, 1950 to April 27, 1951) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include [[person|lurene-tuttle|Lurene Tuttle]] (performer), [[person|howard-duff|Howard Duff]] (performer), Steve Dunne (performer), and Sandra Gould (performer).

The stories often return to private-eye investigation, theft, robbery and stolen property, money, valuables and financial motive, deception, impersonation and hidden identity, romance, jealousy and relationships, and murder and homicide.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Postwar hard-boiled detective boom, Sam Spade character-rights litigation, Network migration from ABC to CBS to NBC, and 1950 Red Channels controversy and cast/sponsor break.
